name: Everest Base Camp Trek
summary: The standard walk in from Lukla through Namche Bazaar and Tengboche to the tents below the Khumbu Icefall, with most itineraries adding the dawn climb of Kala Patthar for the view of Everest itself. The difficulty is altitude and consecutive walking days rather than terrain; no climbing skills are needed.

name: Everest Base Camp via Gokyo Lakes
summary: A loop that reaches base camp by way of the Gokyo valley, taking in the lakes and Gokyo Ri (5,357 m) before crossing the Cho La (5,420 m) to join the main Khumbu trail at Dzongla. Longer and higher than the standard route, with a glaciated pass and a section over the Ngozumpa moraine.

name: Everest Three Passes Trek
summary: A circuit of the upper Khumbu linking the Kongma La (5,535 m), the Cho La (5,420 m) and the Renjo La (5,360 m), usually taking in Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar and the Gokyo lakes on the way round. Several days involve long crossings above 5,300 m and the Cho La has a short glacier section.

name: Gokyo Lakes Trek
summary: An out-and-back up the Dudh Koshi's western branch from Namche through Dole and Machhermo to the string of glacial lakes at Gokyo, with the ascent of Gokyo Ri (5,357 m) as the high point. Quieter than the base camp trail and shorter, but the altitude profile is much the same.

name: Gokyo–Renjo La Trek
summary: The Gokyo valley walked as a loop, returning west over the Renjo La (5,360 m) to Lungden and the Thame valley rather than back down the way it came. The Renjo La is the lowest of the three Khumbu passes and the only one with no glacier on it.

name: Cho La Pass Trek
summary: Sold as the link between the two main Khumbu valleys: the Cho La (5,420 m) is crossed between Dzongla and Thagnak, joining the Everest Base Camp trail to the Gokyo lakes. Most published itineraries are the same loop as the Gokyo variant of the base camp trek, named after its crossing; the pass carries a short section of glacier and can hold ice.

name: Everest View Trek
summary: A short lower-Khumbu walk from Lukla to Namche Bazaar, the Syangboche ridge and the Hotel Everest View (3,880 m), with most versions continuing to Tengboche monastery (about 3,860 m) before turning back. It stays well below the altitudes that make the longer Khumbu routes hard.

name: Ama Dablam Base Camp Trek
summary: The Everest trail as far as Pangboche, then a side branch up the meadows to Ama Dablam's base camp at about 4,570 m. Shorter and lower than the base camp treks further up the valley, and off the main trail for its final two days.

name: Everest High Passes & Island Peak Trek
summary: The three-pass circuit with an ascent of Island Peak (Imja Tse, 6,189 m) added from Chhukung. Unlike the other routes here this one is not walking alone: the summit day involves crampons, a harness and fixed rope on the headwall, and the passes are used as acclimatisation for it.

name: Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek
summary: The original approach walked before the Lukla airstrip, starting at Jiri and crossing the ridges and valleys of the Solu — the Lamjura La (3,530 m) and Taksindu La (about 3,075 m) among them — before joining the usual Khumbu trail at Surke or Phakding. It adds roughly a week of low-altitude climbing and descending, and acclimatises far better than flying in.
